notes: Captain flows require identified Telegram user, consent, role = captain, and non-empty team_id.
Manual report target participant is reloaded by participant_id and checked against captain team_id on start, status selection, step selection, text append, and finalization.
Forged other-team selected participant IDs are rejected server-side.
Forbidden responses do not include other-team participant names, team IDs, or participant IDs.
Dropped participants, duplicates, late finalization, and invalid or closed green steps are rejected before final weekly report writes.
Rejected attempts create no weekly_reports rows, weekly_report_steps rows, or planned step closure side effects in covered tests.
Missing data and unknown user technical details route through NotificationRouter as TECHNICAL_ERROR to admin error bot only.
No production secrets or credentials were introduced by captain-flows.
Search hits for token/credential strings are existing configuration code, tests with dummy values, and documentation references.
CaptainService does not build SQL directly.
pyproject.toml has no runtime dependencies and only pytest as a dev dependency.
No live SDK, deploy, Google, Telegram, OpenAI, Redis, Celery, Docker, or PDF runtime dependency was added by captain-flows.

findings.description: Forbidden captain manual report attempts, such as forged other-team participant IDs, are safely denied but not sent to admin error chat.
findings.impact: This does not expose data or allow unauthorized writes. It may reduce visibility into repeated callback tampering attempts during production operations.
findings.recommendation: If production abuse monitoring becomes necessary, add rate-limited operational/security notifications for repeated forbidden selections without including participant report text or secrets.
